correctness.rationale: The proof derives unique interval/normal-subgroup data for every ordinary congruence, establishes the maximum-preserving iff all subgroups coincide, proves the full automorphism action and orbit formula, and gives the theta density via dominated convergence with a fixed-prime/fixed-chain quantifier. Theta samples are diagnostic, not proof.

originality.rationale: Furlani 2026 defines the enriched signature and proves general classification criteria, but the inspected sections do not give a formula for the chain–group example. Classical band-of-groups congruence theory provides broad machinery; Gaussian flag counting and its theta asymptotics are already known (Kousidis Theorem 3.2). These are expressly not claimed as standalone novelties. No inspected source gives the joint ordinary/enriched normal form, orbit counts, and the contrast of the two prevalence rates for this family. Residual risk: the structural statement may be an unstated short corollary of general Clifford-congruence results.
residual_risks: Classical strong-semilattice-of-groups congruence theorems may make the finite-group normal form a direct specialization.
Kousidis 2011/2013 already proves the generalized-Galois theta asymptotics, so those limits are not original separately.
Spitznagel 1973 and some older Clifford-congruence sources were available only as abstracts; complete texts might yield a stronger implicit corollary.
Searches cannot certify universal historical priority.

value.rationale: The enriched signature forces a natural restriction on congruences introduced in F-inverse monoid research. This theorem quantifies the restriction for every finite chain–group product and finds a genuine difference between raw density (quadratic exponential decay in elementary-abelian rank) and symmetry-orbit density (polynomial decay), with exact finite parameter counts. The finding is a structured infinite-family classification, not an arbitrary isolated slice. It does not claim the previously known generalized-Galois theta constants as novel.
